confidence_limits: Two separate confidences, deliberately not averaged. (A) Confidence in the NO-GO itself is about 97. It rests on EV-001, which was reproduced at runtime twice: meera-run booted the RC, and the verifier ran a standalone Spring bean-factory probe against the RC's own bytecode. That gives E5/C98, and EV-001 alone means a deploy of this RC takes the whole backend down. No other finding needs to be right for NO-GO to hold. (B) Confidence that this register is a complete and correctly-weighted readiness picture is about 75, at evidence level 3. What holds it there: (1) Because EV-001 prevents boot, no end-to-end runtime proof of any money, auth or API flow exists for this RC. Six of the eight surviving P0s (EV-002, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008) and EV-015 are code-trace only (E3-E4), with no request ever sent. (2) The audit sandbox had no Docker, so all 22 Testcontainers integration tests skipped, including EscrowReleaseGateIntegrationTest and DatabaseConstraintIntegrationTest. No agent pulled real GitHub Actions run history (Kavya's systemic gap), so CI status on the RC is inferred from YAML, not observed. (3) Several green money tests mock the exact layer where the bug lives (EV-011, EV-014, EV-025), so the 3621/3621 pass rate is weak evidence for money correctness. (4) Live production env values were not inspected: the VPS .env, GitHub vars, the RazorpayX account and the untracked /usr/local/App/docker-compose.prod.yml. EV-010's live-edge claims are therefore unverified (downgraded to E2/C30). (5) The main working tree is dirty and diverges from the RC under concurrent sessions: F-0848 is uncommitted (EV-018), and the fixes for EV-008 landed after the RC in e67dc5b/1f1bf9f. So the RC is not what main will ship next. (6) Findings are sampled and uneven: 21 agents covered different depths, zara findings carry default E2/C50, and FE coverage was sampled. (7) The following disagreements are recorded and unresolved, not averaged. EV-003 evidence: verifier E4 vs Priya E3. EV-015 severity: verifier P0 vs Kabir/Rohan P1; the decision uses P0. EV-007 evidence: verifier E3 vs Rohan/Tejas E5. EV-099: register P2 vs Kabir P1. EV-144: register P3 vs Rohan/Tejas P1. EV-047: register P2 vs Kavya P3. EV-038 framing: this is a local-sandbox skip, not proof that CI never ran the tests. EV-119 framing: CI has no lint gate at all (XR-KAVYA-01). EV-018: it is main-tree scope, not an RC defect. EV-026 is UNRESOLVED/out of RC scope. EV-034 is REFUTED and dropped.

rationale: NO-GO on RC 115f698. First and decisive, the backend cannot start. EV-001 was reproduced at runtime in two independent ways, so deploying this RC takes down every brand, creator, admin, payment, webhook and Meera path. That alone ends the question, and it is why the NO-GO has much higher confidence than the rest of the audit. LIMITED-BETA-ONLY is not available either, because a beta also needs a backend that boots. Second, even with boot fixed, the money core is not safe to put real brand or creator money through. Verification confirmed a double-fund path (EV-002), a brand self-refund after approved work that applies to every milestone (EV-015), a publish path that skips escrow and fees (EV-005), and a VIEWER-triggered release that is hidden only because approval-release is itself broken (EV-021 masked by EV-019). Third, the site currently tells customers something false and regulated: that an RBI-authorized PA holds their funds and that we never pool (EV-007, XR-ROHAN-01). This directly breaks our own F-0851 rule, and I want it corrected on the live site now, whatever happens to this RC. Fourth, live-format provider keys sit in git history (EV-006); rotating them is a same-day action. What this gets us: by fixing the 8 surviving P0s and the sequenced P1s, cutting a clean RC from committed code, and proving boot plus one full money cycle on staging with executed tests rather than analysis, we can run a controlled invite-only beta with money-out off and affiliate off. That beta would test the real business assumptions (take rate, ops load) without betting the company's regulatory standing or creators' money on code that has never run end to end. The verdicts were applied as instructed: EV-034 dropped as refuted, EV-026 excluded as uncommitted and unresolved, final severities used throughout, and every reviewer disagreement recorded rather than averaged.
